_note: "Try a comparison" (ADR 0100): ready-made scenarios in a row of links above the cards on the Compare page. Each link is the existing shareable address (?s=…, config/view.json share), so it also works opened in a new tab; a plain click swaps the cards in place. Label text: i18n key preset.<id>. Every time is inside the frozen tables (config/ephemeris.json start/stop) and on the hourly grid; the answers each pair shows were measured on 15 Nov 2026 with the page's own rule (centre of the disc against the LOLA skyline) and are written in _answers (S/s = Sun yes/no, E/e = Earth yes/no). tests/presets.test.mjs checks sites, times, count and that both cards of a pair differ in at least one answer. jump_to_earth_view: after loading, the page jumps to the first card's view toward Earth (same as the one-kilometre example button, ADR 0033).

presets._answers: SE → sE: two weeks later the same site has lost its sunlight (Sun 4.1° → −0.2°), Earth still in view
SE → sE: the nominal area is lit, where Odysseus came to rest (about 3 km away) is in shadow
sE vs Se: night at Tranquility Base while the Shackleton ridge is lit but cannot see Earth
Se → se: same ridge, half a year apart; Sun above the skyline 100 % of the hours in Nov 2026, 45 % in May 2027

SE → sE: a lunar eclipse at the south pole (ADR 0109); the Sun stays about 6.3° above the IM-2 skyline, but at 07:00 Earth covers 54 % of it, centre included (NASA GSFC: penumbral lunar eclipse, greatest 07:15 TD on 17 Aug 2027)
